question: Why did iZotope build Nectar 5 around a plugin that reads the sung lyrics and an assistant that designs the vocal chain?

rungs.question: Why did iZotope add Moments, a plugin that puts effects on single sung words?
rungs.answer: Both iZotope and MusicRadar describe it as a way to add small effects to a word or phrase, such as a delay throw on the last word of a chorus, without setting up automation across several plugins.

evidence.quote: Some of the best vocal details are tiny: a delay throw on the last word of the chorus, a harmony that shows up for one line, a reverse swell into the hook. They're also the ones that tend to take an hour of automation tweaking.
it’s a fast and intuitive way to spice up a vocal with effects without getting into the weeds with automation across multiple plugins

counter.text: The "hour of automation tweaking" figure is iZotope's own claim in its launch post; MusicRadar repeats the framing but gives no measurement of its own. Scope: the three sources given.

rungs.question: Why does an effect on one word normally take so much automation work?
rungs.answer: A normal plugin processes the whole track as it plays, so changing an effect for one word means drawing automation lanes that switch it on and off at exactly the right times, often on several plugins. Moments replaces those lanes with a text selection.

evidence.quote: Exactly where you want them. All without managing multiple automation lanes.
rather than working on a stream of real-time audio that’s coming in through the DAW’s playback.

counter.text: None of the sources explains step by step how producers do this by hand today; the link between real-time processing and automation lanes is drawn from the two quotes, not stated in one place. Scope: the three sources given.

rungs.mechanism_type: the software model (real-time stream processing versus timeline editing)

rungs.question: Why can Moments work on words when an ordinary plugin cannot?
rungs.answer: Moments is an ARA plugin: it reads and edits the audio on the DAW's timeline directly, transcribes it into lyrics there, and lets the producer highlight words like text and apply one of seven effects to that span.

evidence.quote: (Moments is an ARA plugin, meaning that it can edit audio on the timeline directly, rather than working on a stream of real-time audio that’s coming in through the DAW’s playback.)

It transcribes your vocal right on your DAW's timeline, so you can highlight words the same way you'd select text in a document, nudge the edges with waveform handles, and add an effect to just that part.

counter.text: It works only where the DAW supports ARA, and iZotope notes limits: "in Logic Pro, ARA currently runs on Intel or under Rosetta only, and in REAPER, ARA works in the VST3 format." No source reports how accurate the transcription is.

rungs.mechanism_type: the software model (ARA timeline access plus lyric transcription)

rungs.question: Why does the same release also have Vocal Assistant design the whole processing chain?
rungs.answer: iZotope pitches Nectar 5 as getting a raw take to a finished vocal whichever way the producer works: Vocal Assistant listens to part of the vocal and builds a chain in one click, and the new Custom Flow lets a producer steer it with style, key, intensity, modules or a reference a cappella.

evidence.quote: This AI-powered mixing tool listens to a portion of your vocal and designs a customized processing chain to match it.
Vocal Assistant has been retuned and can still build your whole chain in one click, which is a great way to get a solid starting point fast. But sometimes you already know where you want to end up.

counter.text: MusicRadar's claim that the assistant was "calibrated to deliver superior results" carries no test or listening comparison, and the product page's "Trained on pro vocal standards" does not say what it was trained on. Scope: the three sources given.

rungs.mechanism_type: the product model (automatic default with user steering)

rungs.question: Why did iZotope launch it at $179 until 7 December, then $249?
rungs.answer: The sources only tie the price to iZotope's Cyber Season sale ending 7 December 2026 and note the company's new owner, Boris FX. None says why that price or why this moment; the commercial reasoning is not in anything read.

evidence.quote: iZotope Nectar 5 is available now at an introductory price of $179 as part of its Cyber Season sale through December 7, after which it’ll cost $249.
even better during our Cyber Sale, ending December 7, 2026.

counter.text: none found; scope: the three sources given, none of which discusses pricing strategy or sales.

landing.shows: The sources show the mechanism: a plugin with direct timeline access (ARA) turns a transcribed vocal into selectable text, so a per-word effect becomes a text selection instead of automation lanes, while Vocal Assistant offers a one-click chain a producer can steer. Why the price and timing were chosen is not in the record.
landing.open_question: When a vocal can be edited as words on a page, does the producer's work move from the waveform to the lyric sheet?
